manual.title: Add OneMeter by address
manual.description: No OneMeter device was discovered by your Bluetooth proxies. Enter the BLE MAC address manually (format: AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF).

credentials.title: OneMeter credentials
credentials.description:
Enter the AES key (mobKey) and IV for device {name} ({address}). These 16-byte values are stored in the device's flash and must be extracted via SWD. See the project README for instructions.

Choose the meter protocol the device should use to read your meter. If you don't know yet, leave it as 'Leave unchanged' — you can set it later from the device's Configure page. Selecting a non-default value writes to the device's flash.

Are you a prosumer (you also feed energy back to the grid, e.g. solar)? This only affects which sensors are enabled by default and can be changed later from the device's Configure page.

The optional passive key/IV pair is also stored in the device's flash (the same extraction tool reads it). With these the integration can decode the device's broadcast advertisements, and while those keep arriving it stays off the GATT link entirely — which extends battery life substantially. Leave both blank to read everything over GATT as before.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-enter OneMeter credentials
reauth_confirm.description:
The current credentials for {name} ({address}) are no longer accepted. Re-enter the AES key and IV.

The passive key/IV fields are optional: leave them blank to keep the pair already stored, or enter a single '-' to remove it.

error.passive_pair_incomplete: Passive reading needs both the passive key and the passive IV — fill in both, or leave both blank.

abort.not_supported: Device does not look like a OneMeter (name does not start with 'OM ').
abort.no_devices_found: No OneMeter devices were found by your Bluetooth proxies. Ensure a proxy is in range and the device is advertising.

init.title: OneMeter — options
init.description:
Each poll wakes the BLE radio, logs in, reads the device, and disconnects. The default 1 hour cadence gives roughly 12 months on the CR2032 battery. Shorter intervals significantly shorten battery life. Allowed range: {min_s}–{max_s} seconds. Press the "Poll now" button to refresh between scheduled polls.

Changing the meter protocol writes to the device's flash on the next poll. 'Leave unchanged' is the safe default — the integration won't touch the device's protocol setting.

Are you a prosumer (you also feed energy back to the grid, e.g. solar)? Enables the Energy export total sensor by default for new installs. Most installs should leave this unchecked. If that sensor was already created and disabled, checking this box now won't un-hide it automatically — enable it once under Settings → Devices & Services → Entities.

'Read data passively' keeps the integration off the GATT link while the device's advertisements are being decoded, and connects again once they go quiet. It needs the device's passive key/IV — a different pair from the AES key/IV, read by tools/extract_credentials.py and entered below. Currently {passive_state}. Leave both fields blank to keep what is stored; enter a single '-' to remove the pair. They are never shown here once saved.
